deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics: no formulas, derivations or computations. It is a set of programmatic notes, apparently for a lecture or memorandum on mathematical teaching and research. It continues the previous page's metaphor of two 'giants' (the concept of magnitude and the concept of decomposition) fighting with weapons (irrational number, ideal). The next page outlines a teaching programme (algebra, geometry and its axioms, training future teachers, preserving rigour).

The content, point by point:
(1) Only a secure stock of knowledge gives the sharpest and farthest-reaching weapons. 'We did not march against France with bow and arrow, although those too would have done some damage', an allusion to 1870/71: modern tools beat obsolete ones even if the old ones still work somewhat.
(2) Programmatic slogans:
- restriction of the material ('Beschränkung des Stoffes');
- historical development kept in the background;
- 'economy of memory' ('Oekonomie des Gedächtnisses'), close to Mach's 'Denkökonomie'.
To carry out these ideas one must resolve to throw away a lot of the rubbish ('Quark').
(3) Science is something living, transmissible by the word, both written and spoken. Whoever knows science only from books knows only a part. Because secondary-school teachers lack oral guidance, their (research) work is unfruitful. The path of oral and personal transmission must come more to the fore.
(4) Personal remark: 'How much have I myself learned through Hurwitz and Minkowski.'

Nothing here can be reconstructed mathematically.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics. Orthographic slips in the original: 'Gedächnisses' for 'Gedächtnisses'; 'Gymnasiallehren' for 'Gymnasiallehrern' (dative plural).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely pedagogical and programmatic. Hilbert's debt to Hurwitz and Minkowski and his emphasis on oral transmission are well documented. The France/bow-and-arrow metaphor and the 'Quark' remark are colourful unpublished details of minor historical interest only.
transcription_corrections: 'Gymnasiallehren' — the intended word is 'Gymnasiallehrern' (dative plural). The ending is cramped in the image; the [?] can likely be resolved this way.
'sichrer[?]' — the image supports 'sichrer' (= sicherer); the [?] can be dropped.
'Gedächnisses' is a faithful reading of the manuscript's misspelling of 'Gedächtnisses'.

'lebendiges.' — the full stop/colon after 'lebendiges' is more likely a colon or hyphen-like mark continuing into 'durch das Wort übertragbares'. The sentence reads 'Die Wissenschaft ist etwas lebendiges, durch das Wort übertragbares, ...'.
